concepts_present.evidence_quote: We frame object detection as a single regression problem ... a single neural network predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities.
We use non-maximal suppression to fix these multiple detections.
Our loss function is a sum-squared error over coordinates, confidence, and class probabilities.

concepts_absent.rationale: YOLO removes the region-proposal stage entirely; detection is done in one network pass over the full image.
YOLOv1 predicts boxes directly per grid cell without using anchor priors (anchors first appeared in YOLOv2).
YOLO does not use bipartite matching or set-prediction objectives; it relies on per-cell prediction + NMS.
YOLOv1 uses convolutional + fully-connected layers, not transformers.
YOLOv1 predates focal loss; it uses sum-squared error reweighting for the no-object case.
No ROI extraction step in YOLO.
YOLOv1 is a detection-only model; no segmentation branch.
YOLOv1 features are learned by a Darknet-like CNN; no HOG/SIFT-style handcrafted descriptors.
